newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close mixed, Dec up on basis trade.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close mixed, Dec up on basis trade.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mixed with spot December up and other months ending lower but with pared losses by the close. Feeder cattle also ended mixed, following live cattle, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.125 cent a lb higher to 0.225 lower with December up most and February off 0.150 at 62.750 cents.

Ideas the December live cattle contract should move to a premium basis to cash pushed that month higher late while short covering pared early losses in deferreds, partly reflecting a somewhat better tone to cash cattle prices.

"We are in that time frame when you have to look at what basis this December deserves to have, and in most cases people would agree that it probably will end up going off the board at a slight premium to the cash," said Tom Tippens, CEO Professional Cattle Consultants Inc.

Tippens noted that in recent expirations of live cattle futures contracts, some months went off the board with as much as a 2.000- to 3.000-cent premium to cash. Cash will likely stabilize at $66 per cwt, he said.
Deferred months were depressed early by forecasts for increasing cattle numbers but losses were pared by short covering.
Expectations are that the monthly Cattle-on-Feed report, due out December 20, will show more cattle on feed than a year ago.
But futures recovered somewhat as February already holds a large discount to current cash levels and a current marketing pace may continue, traders said.
"If we keep selling cattle as aggressively as we have, you won't see the market get that cheap," Tippens added.
Refco and RBH bought February light and Prudential Securities remained a good buyer in December. Prudential also spread long August/short April early, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, Dean Witter and LIT division of First Options bought February 66 calls at the close. Volatility was steady to firm, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle continued to follow the lead of live cattle and recovered late to end mixed. A lower CME feeder cattle index also weighed on prices early before futures turned up after holding technical support above the 40-day moving average, traders said.
The latest index was off $1.00 at $64.53 per cwt.
Feeders closed 0.125 cent a lb lower to 0.075 higher with only January off at 65.975 cents.
